q: The U.S.-China tariff truce is extended again before it expires or is replaced by a comprehensive agreement
basis: Reciprocal state visits by the U.S. and Chinese leaders in May and September established a framework of strategic stability, and Xi Jinping has said the two should meet again soon. The U.S. Russia sanctions law (the Graham Act), which took effect on September 18, mandates tariffs from October 18 on major buyers of Russian oil and gas and could have collided with the U.S.-China truce had China been targeted, but President Trump waived those tariffs on October 16. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president would review the effects for up to 60 days. On November 9, China extended its suspension of trade countermeasures and tariffs against the U.S., along with its pause on rare earth export controls (Reuters).
rs: Announcements by the White House or USTR and by China's Ministry of Commerce
